result:
I calculated the 2025 Q3 results and saved them to `/work/answer.json`. With the same rules, the 2025 Q2 run matched all 10 of your reference values exactly.

| Item | Q3 value |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | enterprise, 294,497,215 KRW |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 249 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | sw, 289,964,925 KRW |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-07 |
| e. Customer with the largest refund total | u239@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders | 235 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 692,323 KRW |
| h. Growth from August to September | 4.1% |

Your definitions didn't cover three data issues. I went with the choices that reproduced the Q2 values:

- **Time zone:** `ordered_at` is stored in UTC (it ends in `Z`). I converted it to Korean time (UTC+9) before splitting by quarter and month. Using UTC as stored gave different Q2 results; for example, d came out as 2025-06 and h as 7.8.
- **Duplicate customers:** there are 300 customer IDs but only 250 distinct emails. I counted one email as one customer. Counting by ID gave b = 273 and f = 218 for Q2, which don't match the reference.
- **Segment labels:** variants like `consumer`, ` consumer` and `Enterprise ` are written inconsistently. I trimmed spaces and lowercased them so each segment is grouped once.

STATUS: DONE
